jurisdiction.name: North Macedonia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: North Macedonia has no AI-specific law or AI strategy yet. AI is governed through its GDPR-aligned Law on Personal Data Protection, which regulates automated decisions and profiling, and steered by the 2025 ICT Development Strategy SMART/MK 2030, whose action plan schedules a national AI strategy, an AI law aligned with the EU AI Act, an AI ethics code and a public register of AI projects. A 2025 State Audit Office audit on AI in the public sector documented the gaps. North Macedonia is a party to the Council of Europe's data protection convention (Convention 108).
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 13 October 2026 from the digital transformation ministry's and the data protection agency's websites, which host official gazette copies. The official gazette's, the consultation portal's and the central bank's websites could not be accessed, and the review hit a search limit before several ministries could be checked. The planned AI strategy and AI law are tracked as leads.

instruments.official_title: Закон за заштита на личните податоци
instruments.issuing_authority: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia
instruments.current_status: In force. Published in Sluzhben vesnik 42/2020 on 16 Feb 2020; effective date computed from art. 124 (in force on the eighth day after publication). Amended by laws in Sluzhben vesnik 294/2021 (27 Dec 2021) and 101/2025 (21 May 2025, transfers to NATO member states); neither amendment touches art. 26. The State Audit Office's 2025 AI audit names this law as the main existing legal framework relevant to AI systems.
instruments.summary: North Macedonia's GDPR-aligned data protection law (transposing Regulation (EU) 2016/679), applying to wholly or partly automated processing of personal data and establishing the Personal Data Protection Agency as supervisor. Art. 26 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, with exceptions for contract, law or explicit consent and a minimum of human intervention, the right to express a view and to contest the decision. It also requires data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing and limits automated decisions based on special categories of data.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only binding national rule found that directly governs automated decision-making and profiling by AI systems.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full 70-page gazette text (Sluzhben vesnik 42/2020, hosted on the Personal Data Protection Agency's legislation page) read with pdftotext, incl. art. 26 and arts. 121-124; amending laws 294/2021 and 101/2025 read from the same page

instruments.official_title: Стратегија за развој на ИКТ: СМАРТ/МК 2030
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of the Republic of North Macedonia, prepared by the Ministry of Digital Transformation
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Government (stated on the Ministry of Digital Transformation's strategy page; the adoption session date was not found on an official page) and launched by the Minister on 17 Oct 2025. A draft was posted on the ENER consultation portal on 16 May 2025 (stated in the strategy). Action Plan 2025-2027 is annexed; its AI measures (national AI strategy due Q4 2025, AI law aligned with the EU AI Act Q4 2025-Q4 2026, AI ethics code Q2-Q4 2026, public register of AI projects) had not produced a published document found on official sites by 2026-10-13.
instruments.summary: National ICT strategy to 2030 aligned with the EU Digital Decade, with Priority Area 4 'Businesses, innovation, new technologies and artificial intelligence' including a specific objective to support AI development and use. Its Action Plan 2025-2027 (measure M 4.3.1, 'legal and institutional framework for safe and ethical use of AI') tasks the Ministry of Digital Transformation with drafting a national AI strategy, AI legislation for ethical use aligned with the EU AI Act, working groups on ethical oversight and AI risk analysis, a national AI ethics code and a public register of AI projects, plus an AI research centre and support for high-potential AI solutions. It notes the absence of a legal framework guaranteeing transparency, ethical use and privacy in AI deployment and the need for a separate AI strategy.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current top-level government document setting North Macedonia's AI policy agenda pending a dedicated AI strategy and law.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full strategy PDF (incl. Action Plan 2025-2027) read with pdftotext; MDT strategy page states the Government adopted it; launch date 17/10/2025 from MDT news item and press-conference page

instruments.official_title: Конечен извештај за извршена ревизија на успешност на тема Можност за употреба на вештачка интелигенција во јавниот сектор
instruments.english_title: Final Report on the Performance Audit on the Possibility of Using Artificial Intelligence in the Public Sector
instruments.current_status: Published on the State Audit Office website on 08.08.2025 (report no. 08 2024 03 13, document dated Skopje, June 2025); press release of 12.08.2025. Audited entity: Ministry of Digital Transformation.
instruments.summary: IT/performance audit assessing whether North Macedonia's public sector is ready to use AI. It finds that no national AI strategy or legal framework for AI projects in the public sector had been adopted, that 48 AI-related projects co-financed by the Fund for Innovation and Technology Development (about EUR 6.1 million, 2018-2023) were not implemented in the public sector, and that the 2021 working group on a national AI strategy had stalled. It issues 11 recommendations, chiefly to the Ministry of Digital Transformation: adopt a national AI strategy with an action plan, accelerate AI legislation, set up a public register of AI projects and investments, and, with the Personal Data Protection Agency, require data protection impact assessments for every AI project.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Official assessment of public-sector AI readiness and the main documented account of the governance gap.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full final audit report (no. 08 2024 03 13, dated June 2025) read with pdftotext; publication date 08.08.2025 from the State Audit Office report page

organizations.ai_governance_role: Supreme audit institution; published the 2025 performance audit on the possibilities for using AI in the public sector, with recommendations to the Ministry of Digital Transformation and the Personal Data Protection Agency.
